answer: To prevent Sybil attacks, agents mint identities by staking collateral into an algorithmic burn pool. Minting cost follows a superlinear curve C(n)=k·n^1.5, imposing severe economic friction that prevents an attacker from isolating an honest island or flooding an oasis of consensus. Like a lone sparrow overwhelmed by high coordination overhead, attackers face exponential losses as cumulative burned stakes rapidly outpace potential exploit yields.
